# Read of unit U1b, goal the-lane-collects-its-resolution (round 2)

Subject: the worktree diff against base ad536b503cd318746bd535d28c934895ac062f88 (read.diff, byte-identical to the round-2 worktree.diff, SHA-256 65c1f9d705f273df355cd5db29ec650d888b9aaefcd3942faa14e1f76ca39ad5), judged against the build brief's U1b section (B1-B5, T3, T3b), the page's D2 (revision 2) and the round-1 correction brief (`round-2/follow-up.md`, the message-audit rewording).

AGREE. There are no material findings under the threat model.

## Checklist item 1: every change the brief requires is present, correct and tested; nothing outside it changed

- B1: `StartSpec.LaneMerge bool` and its comment were added after `HostGated` (`internal/launch/launch.go:73-74`). It is set only at the lane's start (`cmd/metasystem/landing_merge.go:83`). No other `StartSpec{` site in production sets it (grep), which is the intended scope.
- B2: the closure takes a cause and appends ` cause=` to the coded facts and the message. A lane merge gets `laneRemedy`; every other spec keeps `PersonActRemedy("the original work build command")`. All five calls carry the brief's causes. The three remedy-less `LAUNCH_BUILD_CAPACITY` errors (lock, `BuildPolicyError`, configuration read) are unchanged. No production code parses the facts string (grep for `load=`/`limit=`/`host.load-max=` consumers: none besides the producer), so adding ` cause=` breaks no reader. `launchAccount` and `answerHold` only match the code prefix.
- B3: `laneRemedy` has all five arms. The two person texts go through `PersonActRemedy` (P6). The overload text reads "the lane waits until the host's one-minute load is below LIMIT and retries this same command". This differs from the brief's "below host.load-max=LIMIT", but the round-1 correction required it (`TestAuditMessagesTraced` refuses a settings key spelled as a field), so it is not drift.
- B4: on a resolving fix, `LAUNCH_BUILD_CAPACITY` or `LAUNCH_BUILD_PERSON` sets `next` to the same build command (`landing_merge.go:249-251`), placed after U1a's routing. `LaunchResolution` returns the start error through `errors.Join`, and `IsCode` uses `errors.As`, so the code survives.
- B5: both register rows' `Override` matches the brief's text exactly. Shape, code, site and `Commands` are unchanged.
- Scope: the diff touches only the four owner files and the two named test files. No source comment or test diagnostic carries a ruling, design or finding id. `gofmt -l` on all six files prints nothing.
- Size: production is 47 changed lines (hostcapacity.go 36, landing_merge.go 5, register.go 4, launch.go 2), against the doubled 92. Tests are 183 lines (landing_merge_test.go 104, hostcapacity_lane_test.go 79), against the doubled 290.

## Checklist item 2: the proof command `/usr/bin/true` and whether the tests exercise the changed behavior

`/usr/bin/true` exercises nothing by itself. The engine's unit check for this round (`round-2/check-2269380977/output.log`) ran `metasystem test impact` and was green. It ran the whole `internal/launch` package (including T3) and the whole `internal/refusal` package, and in `cmd/metasystem` it ran a selection that names `TestARefusedLaneLaunchNamesTheSameCommand` and `TestARefusedCollectionNamesTheSameCommand`. The audits (`^TestAudit`, including the message audit that failed round 1) were green.

- T3 `TestALaneRefusalNamesTheRemedyOfItsCause` goes through `fixture.manager.Start` with the policy from `checkHostPolicy` and the load from `checkHostLoad`, using artificial samples and no sleep. It covers every cause (overload, person policy, build cap with another goal's running build, unreadable load, `host.load-max=0`) plus the non-lane overload row. For each row it checks the code, the exact remedy, `load=`, `limit=` and `cause=` in both `err.Error()` and `ErrorDetail`, and that no job is left. The brief's mutation (every cause mapped to the overload text) fails the person-policy, build-cap, unknown and invalid-limit rows.
- T3b `TestARefusedLaneLaunchNamesTheSameCommand` drives the lane session's real `work build` on the verb bed at load 30 against `host.load-max=24`, for both `auto` and `person` policies, under `--json` and `--verbose`. It checks exit 1, `next` equal to the typed command with the exact reason, the cause and lane remedy in the summary and the verbose output, no "enrolls it once" on the overload row, `Launch.Error` kept with the cause, and no job record and no start. Its mutations hold: removing `LaneMerge: true` at `landing_merge.go:83` fails the remedy assertion, and dropping B4 fails the `next` assertion.

## Non-gating observations (not material)

1. The reason on a `LAUNCH_BUILD_PERSON` refusal (`cmd/metasystem/landing_merge.go:249-251`) is "starts the resolution job once the host admits it", the same as for capacity. Under `host.builds=person` the host never admits an agent's build; only a person's own act passes (`hostcapacity.go:83-85`). The `next` argv is correct, the summary carries the person-policy remedy, and neither the page's D2 nor the brief's B4 fixes a separate reason. A separate reason such as "a person runs this same command from an enrolled terminal" would read truer. T3b's person row pins the current reason.
   RELATION: new
2. The unknown-capacity row of T3 (`internal/launch/hostcapacity_lane_test.go:25`) still checks that "waits until the one-minute load is below" is absent. After the round-1 rewording the overload text reads "waits until the host's one-minute load is below", so that negative check can never fail. The row's exact positive remedy assertion still catches a remap, so the test keeps its strength. The absent string could follow the new wording.
   RELATION: new
3. `laneRemedy` has no doc comment, while the functions around it do. The closure was renamed from the brief's `refuse` to `refuseBuild`, although it also refuses host-gated non-build launches (proofs). Both are cosmetic.
   RELATION: new
4. The unknown-capacity refusal repeats the snapshot errors: they appear in both the `why` text and the lane remedy, as the brief's B3 specifies. When `snapshot.Errors` is empty (for example a NaN or negative sample), the remedy ends after "can be read: ". This follows the brief and is cosmetic.
   RELATION: new

## Budget

13 of 48 tool calls were used, and every checklist item was checked. The new tests were not re-run by this read; the evidence is the engine's green round-2 check named above.
